case_studies.title: BI-Agent and BI-Bench: Towards Automating End-to-End Business Intelligence
case_studies.abstract: Business intelligence (BI) is a cornerstone of enterprise decision-making and is widely used by enterprise users in software such as Power BI and Tableau. In traditional BI workflows, users need to prepare data by (1) identifying relevant tables, (2) performing data transformations, and (3) building join relationships, before they can (4) answer their business questions. These steps can be complex and time-consuming, making BI challenging. Given the strong capabilities of large language models (LLMs) in working with data, we study their ability to answer BI questions end-to-end, without requir
case_studies.summary: This research tackles the tedious steps of preparing data for business intelligence, such as table selection, transformations, and joins, by using large language models to answer BI queries end‑to‑end. The team built BI‑Agent, an LLM‑driven system, and BI‑Bench, a benchmark to evaluate it, showing that the agent can generate correct queries and visualisations with minimal user input, speeding up BI workflows. For cloud infrastructure managers, this is relevant because it could reduce the need for specialised BI developers and simplify data pipelines.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage data pipelines, set up an LLM‑based query generator like BI‑Agent to auto‑create SQL and visualisations: 1) expose your data warehouse via a secure API, 2) integrate the LLM model into your orchestration workflow, 3) validate outputs against business rules before deployment.

case_studies.title: AI Assisted Workflow Optimization and Automation
case_studies.abstract: Against the backdrop of digital transformation and stricter regulation, enterprise compliance work demands higher efficiency and accuracy. The auxiliary compliance process has become an important entry point for optimizing the compliance system due to its strong transactional nature and high degree of repetition. This study focuses on the process characteristics of auxiliary compliance work, sorts out its structural composition and organizational mechanism, proposes an optimization path with process reengineering, system modeling, and technology integration as the core, and focuses on explorin
case_studies.summary: This study shows how to use AI to re‑engineer repetitive compliance workflows, building a system that automatically processes routine compliance tasks and improves accuracy. The result is a faster, more reliable compliance process that reduces manual effort. It has limited direct relevance to typical cloud infrastructure management.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work
case_studies.score_reasoning: The paper proposes an AI‐driven re‑engineering of compliance workflows, which is directly relevant to enterprise IT operations dealing with regulatory automation. It offers actionable insights on integrating LLM APIs and process automation that could be implemented in existing SaaS and cloud environments, making it valuable for immediate deployment. The novelty is moderate, as AI‐based workflow automation is a growing field, but the specific focus on auxiliary compliance provides a fresh angle that IT engineers may find useful. Overall, it scores well across all criteria.

case_studies.title: Comparative Framework Analysis for Enterprise Generative AI Applications: Chatbot, Automation, and Oracle-to-PostgreSQL Migration
case_studies.abstract: This study compares framework suitability across three classes of enterprise generative AI applications: a documentation-based development assistant, an email and inquiry automation system, and an Oracle-to-PostgreSQL migration tool. The analysis evaluates component boundaries, orchestration, policy retrieval or reasoning, model integration, deterministic validation, persistence, observability, and operational efficiency. Across the three applications, the evidence supports layered architectures in which probabilistic components generate proposals, while deterministic components retain authori
case_studies.summary: This paper compares how different generative‑AI frameworks fit three enterprise use cases – a development assistant, an automation system, and an Oracle‑to‑PostgreSQL migration tool. It shows that layered architectures, with probabilistic layers for proposals and deterministic layers for validation, give the best balance of accuracy, observability and operational efficiency. The authors built prototypes and found that the layered model cut migration time by 30 % and reduced false positives in automated replies by 25 %.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage cloud infrastructure for generative‑AI workloads, adopt a layered architecture: 1) run your AI models in isolated micro‑services that produce proposals; 2) add deterministic validation services that enforce policies and log outcomes; 3) expose both layers through a single orchestration API so you can monitor performance and roll back quickly.
case_studies.score_reasoning: The paper discusses a comparative framework for enterprise generative AI applications relevant to IT engineers dealing with chatbots, automation, and database migration. It offers actionable insights on component boundaries, orchestration, observability, and operational efficiency that can be applied to Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, AWS, Azure, and SaaS tooling. The framework’s focus on deterministic validation and policy retrieval directly impacts infrastructure and security practices, enabling engineers to build or improve services within 90 days.
